items.title: Iraqi forces enter Jurf al Sakhar militia stronghold as PM seeks to consolidate power
items.summary: Iraqi security forces entered Jurf al Sakhar, a longstanding stronghold of the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah militia, on November 20 following an investigation into oil smuggling. The continued presence of militia fighters and the deployment of Popular Mobilization Forces brigades raise questions about whether Baghdad can establish full government control over the area. items.title: Trump announces new tariffs on EU, China despite US midterms defeat

China could be slapped with a 20 percent tariff, a senior official said. The announcement came weeks after a cost-of-living crisis landed the Republicans a sweeping defeat in the US midterms.

items.title: Yemen's Houthis claim attacks on Riyadh financial district, Saudi refinery
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis on Wednesday claimed attacks targeting the financial district in the Saudi capital and the sprawling Ras Tanura refinery in the kingdom's oil-rich east, in retaliation for strikes on their territory. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree described the attack targeting the refinery as "accurate and direct", saying it "caused fires to break out at the facility". He said the attack on Riyadh was "carried out in three phases, with strikes hitting their targets accurately".

items.title: Security Council LIVE: Can conflict resolution keep pace as AI and drones reshape war?
items.summary: When the UN was founded in 1945, computers, the internet and satellites were the stuff of science fiction. Today, artificial intelligence (AI) is already assisting in targeting, drones are reshaping warfare and disinformation is spreading in unprecedented ways, fuelling record levels of conflict. The Security Council on Tuesday is weighing these changes, with UN chief António Guterres telling ambassadors, “killer robots must have no place in our future.”
